title: A read that repairs one replica
request:
three replicas, two of them behind, and the same read issued twice

./your_program.sh anti-entropy
init ["r1","r2","r3"]
put r1 k new 5
put r2 k old 2
read k
read k
note: The repair list must be the stale list and nothing more. Writing the winning value back to every replica works, costs three writes instead of two, and hides the very thing the field is there to show you: how far out of step the replicas had drifted.

title: A hint that outlives its holder
request:
a write while r3 is away, then the stand-in holding its hint dies too

./your_program.sh anti-entropy
init ["r1","r2","r3"]
down r3
write k v 1
down r1
up r3
handoff
sync r2 r3
note: Hinted handoff is a latency optimisation wearing the costume of a durability mechanism. The hint is one more copy on one more machine, and when that machine goes, so does it. Only a full comparison between two replicas is a guarantee.
